skill.name: pytest-mock-guide
skill.description: Practical guidance for writing pytest tests with pytest-mock, including patching, spying, stubbing, autospec, assertions, async mocks, and fixture scopes.
skill.summary: Write focused pytest-mock tests with reliable patches, spies, stubs, and call assertions.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: All 91 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, test-only mock examples, and an ordinary ValueError example. The skill contains documentation only, with no command execution, active filesystem behavior, prompt injection, or malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: pytest-mock is a pytest plugin providing a `mocker` fixture as a thin wrapper around Python's `unitt
The `mocker` fixture is the main interface. Request it in your test function:
| `class_mocker` | class | Share mocks across test class |
| `module_mocker` | module | Share mocks across test module |
| `session_mocker` | session | Share mocks across entire session |
Same as `patch.object` but doesn't warn when mock is used as context manager:
| `return_value` | Value returned when mock is called |
| `side_effect` | Exception to raise or function to call |
| `spec_set` | Stricter spec that prevents setting new attributes |
| `spy_return` | Last return value from real method |

content.value_statement: Mocking errors can make Python tests brittle or misleading. This guide provides practical pytest-mock patterns for focused patches, spies, stubs, and assertions.
actual_capabilities: Explains function, class, module, package, and session mocker fixture scopes.
Shows how to patch functions, object attributes, dictionaries, and multiple attributes.
Covers spies, synchronous stubs, asynchronous stubs, and autospecced mocks.
Documents call assertions, await assertions, return values, and side effects.
Provides patterns for built-ins, properties, iterators, callbacks, and async context managers.
Explains mock cleanup, reset, stop, and pytest assertion configuration.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not execute or validate tests.
Assumes pytest and pytest-mock are already installed.
Uses placeholder modules and classes that require adaptation to each project.
Does not cover every unittest.mock or third-party mocking feature.

use_cases.title: Isolate Service Dependencies
use_cases.description: Create focused unit tests that replace database, cache, API, or filesystem dependencies.

use_cases.title: Review Mocking Strategy
use_cases.description: Check patch targets, fixture scopes, assertions, and cleanup choices during test review.

use_cases.title: Teach Advanced Test Patterns
use_cases.description: Demonstrate spies, autospec, side effects, async mocks, and fixture composition with concise examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Patch
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a pytest test for [function] using mocker.patch. Replace [dependency], verify its call, and assert [expected result].

prompt_templates.title: Patch the Correct Namespace
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [module] and show where to patch [dependency]. Explain the import namespace and add precise call assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Test Async Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an async pytest test for [function]. Mock [async dependency], configure its result, and verify awaited arguments.

prompt_templates.title: Design Strict Mock Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design tests for [component] using autospec, side effects, spies, and fixture scopes. Cover success, failure, and call order.

output_examples.input: Test a function that sends one email through a client dependency.
output_examples.output: A focused pytest test patches the imported client, sets a successful result, and verifies one call with the expected recipient.

output_examples.input: Verify an async repository lookup without contacting the database.
output_examples.output: An async test replaces the repository method, configures its return value, awaits the service, and checks the awaited arguments.

output_examples.input: Review a failing patch that targets the dependency definition.
output_examples.output: The review identifies the consumer module namespace as the correct patch target and recommends an autospecced mock with a precise assertion.

best_practices: Patch objects where the tested module imports and uses them.
Use autospec or spec_set when interface accuracy matters.
Assert meaningful interactions and returned behavior without testing implementation details.
anti_patterns: Do not patch the definition namespace when the consumer imported the object directly.
Do not share mutable mock state across tests without deliberate fixture scope management.
Do not replace every collaborator when a small real object would make the test clearer.

faq.question: What does pytest-mock add to pytest?
faq.answer: It provides the mocker fixture, automatic cleanup, pytest-friendly assertion messages, and access to unittest.mock helpers.

faq.question: Where should I patch a dependency?
faq.answer: Patch the name in the module where the tested code looks it up.

faq.question: When should I use mocker.spy?
faq.answer: Use a spy when real behavior should run while calls, returns, or exceptions are recorded.

faq.question: How do I mock asynchronous functions?
faq.answer: Patch the async dependency, configure its return value, and verify interactions with await assertions.

faq.question: Why should I use autospec?
faq.answer: Autospec constrains the mock to the target interface and catches invalid method calls or arguments.

faq.question: Does the guide modify project files?
faq.answer: No. It contains documentation examples and does not execute tests or modify files.
